name: Ca' Foscari University of Venice
summary: Public university in Venice; eight English bachelor's in business, economics, computing, tourism and humanities, most with limited places.

ib.text: A school-leaving diploma after 12 years that gives university access at home. Limited-place degrees add an entry test; English level is set on each programme's page.

lastYear.text: 2026-27: entry-test degrees by 22 July; open by 14 October

programmes.name: Business Administration and Management
programmes.about: Business administration and management taught in English in Venice, with double-degree options.
programmes.overview: You learn business economics, accounting, marketing and law, then look at how organisations take decisions, handle finance and banking, read balance sheets and use budgeting and planning tools. The course is practice-oriented, with project work, real business cases, design thinking, role plays and guest speakers from industry, and you work with companies from the first year. Sustainability, tourism, food and beverage and culture feature as sectors. Exchange and internships abroad are possible, and a double degree with Toulouse School of Management is on offer. Graduates go into management and consulting, sales, banking, finance, public administration, human resources and marketing.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Digital Management
programmes.about: Management for the digital economy, taught in English at Ca' Foscari's Roncade campus.
programmes.overview: The degree covers four linked areas: economics and digital law, digital technology such as IT systems, networks and big data, organisation and strategy for innovation with AI, blockchain and Industry 4.0, and marketing and communication built on data and e-commerce. Classes are held with the H-FARM College, which brings entrepreneurship into the academic work. You learn through projects, lab work, workshops with business leaders, networking events, business challenges and guest sessions, with internship support from the career service. Graduates work as digital managers, business analysts, innovation or project managers, data analysts, marketing and e-commerce specialists, or found their own start-ups.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Economics and Business
programmes.about: Economics and business taught in English in Venice.
programmes.overview: The degree blends economics, law, quantitative analysis and business management, with attention to financial systems and markets and to global economic challenges. Teaching builds specialist and soft skills together, and you can study or intern abroad through Erasmus+ and overseas exchanges, or do a training internship in Italy through the career service. Graduates go into companies, public institutions and international organisations, working for instance as economic or financial consultants, market analysts and financial specialists in banking, or they continue to postgraduate study.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Computer Science (Data Science curriculum)
programmes.about: Computer science at the Mestre science campus; the degree runs in Italian and English, with a Data Science curriculum taught in English.
programmes.overview: You learn to design, build and manage systems that generate, transmit and process information, together with statistical methods for analysing data. The English-taught Data Science curriculum focuses on data analysis using statistics and artificial intelligence, alongside two other curricula, one in Italian on software development and a European one with a year abroad and a double degree. Teaching combines theory with laboratory work and company internships, and also covers the legal and ethical side of the profession. Graduates work in software development, data analysis and IT administration in companies, public bodies and research labs, or continue to the English-taught master's in Computer Science and Information Technology.
programmes.ib: Open access. The degree is Italian/English; choose the English-taught Data Science curriculum.
programmes.selectionNote: Open access: meet the entry requirements and you can enrol. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Hospitality Innovation and e-Tourism
programmes.about: Hospitality and tourism combined with digital innovation, taught in English between Venice and Mestre.
programmes.overview: The degree combines three strands: management skills such as finance, human resources, organisation and industry regulation, digital tools such as property management systems, CRM, social media strategy and data analytics, and cultural and territorial knowledge including museology, history and geography. Learning is hands-on, with workshops, labs and three internships, one each year, that move from operational to supervisory roles, with partners such as the Fondazione Scuola Italiana di Ospitalita and TH Resorts. Graduates work as middle managers in hotels, destination management and tourism firms, or in digital marketing and online travel agencies, and some go on to a master's in hospitality or tourism.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Ancient Civilizations for the Contemporary World
programmes.about: An inter-university degree in English on the ancient world and its meaning today, taught between Milan and Venice.
programmes.overview: You study ancient societies across the Mediterranean, the Middle East and Asia, combining social and anthropological analysis, work with source texts, and language and philology, with an eye on how cultures connect and differ. Classes run in a blended format between the Venice and Milan campuses, in person with live streaming and tutors supporting the remote classrooms, as the degree is shared with the University of Milan. Graduates look to museums, archaeological sites and exhibitions, cultural communication, and consulting for the entertainment industry on historical themes, while guiding tourists requires extra postgraduate training.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Italian and Mediterranean Studies
programmes.about: Italian and Mediterranean studies taught in English in Venice; first intake 2026/2027.
programmes.overview: A single curriculum joins language, literature, history, the arts and geopolitics to look at Italy's place in the Mediterranean from ancient to contemporary times, through texts, documents, artworks and social practices. Subjects include Mediterranean history, comparative literature, archaeology and art, intercultural communication and digital scholarship, with optional modules to shape your own path. You can apply what you learn through activities and internships, or study abroad on Erasmus+ and overseas exchanges. Graduates go into museums, cultural organisations, publishing, tourism and international projects, education, content creation and Euro-Mediterranean cooperation.
programmes.selectionNote: Open access: meet the entry requirements and you can enrol. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

programmes.name: Philosophy, International and Economic Studies
programmes.about: Philosophy combined with international and economic studies, taught in English in Venice, with double-degree options.
programmes.overview: Modelled on the Oxford PPE idea, the degree joins philosophy with economics, politics, history and law, pairing a logical and philosophical approach with the social and economic sciences to make sense of global, political and cultural questions. You read demanding texts, learn to put forward solutions to current problems, and attend a public lecture series with visiting scholars. Exchange semesters abroad and internships are available, and a double degree exists with University College Groningen. Graduates work in analysis and consulting, public relations and policy roles in agencies and international bodies, or continue to master's programmes such as Economics and Finance or Comparative International Relations.
programmes.ib: Limited places with an entry test.
programmes.selectionNote: Limited places, filled by an entry test ranking; see the programme's call. 2026 criteria; 2027 not yet published.

notes: Admission for 2027-28 has not opened yet; register on apply.unive.it to be told when your rounds open.
In 2026 EU applicants could apply until 22 July for degrees with an entry test and until 14 October for open-access degrees.
Applicants with a school average of 85% or more can apply for merit scholarships, but only in the first two admission rounds.
